reasoning: The deviations are concentrated in the reactor feed (Stream 6) composition — A and E mole % down ~1%, F up — together with a sharp drop in D in the product (XMEAS_37, -25.8%) and a compensating adjustment of the A and C feed valve (XMV_4), which is the classic signature of a step change in the A/C ratio of Stream 4: more C relative to A drives reaction 1 (A+C+D→G) harder, consuming more D so less D slips through to the stripper underflow while A/E fractions in the feed fall and byproduct F rises. IDV(1) explains all six feature deviations, whereas reactor/condenser cooling faults (IDV(4,5,11,12,14,15)), feed temperature faults (IDV(3,9,10)), or kinetics drift (IDV(13)) would instead show their largest deviations in temperatures, pressures, or coolant variables, which are absent here. Among the remaining candidates, the other Stream 4 composition-related faults IDV(7) and IDV(2) are the closest alternatives, though IDV(2) is less likely because B mole % in the reactor feed is not among the top contributors.
